evidence: src/application/TaskDTO.ts declares `interface TaskDTO { dueDate: string | null; status: TaskStatus; ... }`, but no use case references it
src/application/AddTaskUseCase.ts: `execute(id, projectId, title, description, dueDate: Date | null): Task` returns the domain Task, not a TaskDTO
src/application/CreateProjectUseCase.ts: `execute(id: string, name: string): Project` returns the domain Project, while src/application/ProjectDTO.ts declares `ProjectDTO`, which goes unused
src/application/CreateUserUseCase.ts: `execute(id: string, name: string): User` returns the domain User, while src/application/UserDTO.ts declares `UserDTO`, which goes unused
src/application/ListTasksUseCase.ts, MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts and AssignTaskUseCase.ts all return `Task`/`Task[]` domain entities
AssignTaskUseCase.ts and MarkTaskDoneUseCase.ts both contain `if (!task) { throw new Error(`Task with id ${taskId} not found`); }`
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The six use-case classes are one coherent concern. Each one orchestrates domain entities through their repositories in the same constructor-injection and execute() style. Domain rules stay in the domain: MarkTaskDoneUseCase delegates the done check to task.canMarkDone(), and AssignTaskUseCase delegates to task.withAssignee().

The boundary is not consistent, though. The module declares ProjectDTO, TaskDTO and UserDTO as its data-transfer contracts, yet no use case uses them. Every execute() returns a domain entity (Project, User or Task), so the module's own DTOs are bypassed and domain types leak across the module boundary. The mismatch shows most clearly in TaskDTO: its dueDate is a string, while AddTaskUseCase accepts and returns a Task with a Date. So the conversion between the two shapes is not owned by this module at all and must happen elsewhere, in the calling controllers.

There is also a smaller duplication. The not-found check and its error message ("Task with id ${taskId} not found") are copied into both AssignTaskUseCase and MarkTaskDoneUseCase instead of living in one place. The main reason for failing is the DTO/entity split in the module's boundary abstraction.

violations.message: TaskDTO is declared as the module's task contract, but none of AddTaskUseCase, AssignTaskUseCase, ListTasksUseCase or MarkTaskDoneUseCase uses it. They return the domain Task instead, so the DTO is bypassed and the Date-to-string conversion of dueDate is left outside the module.
ProjectDTO is declared, but CreateProjectUseCase.execute returns the domain Project. The module's DTO is bypassed and a domain entity leaks across the boundary.
UserDTO is declared, but CreateUserUseCase.execute returns the domain User. The module's DTO is bypassed and a domain entity leaks across the boundary.
The task-not-found guard and its error message are copied from AssignTaskUseCase.ts instead of living in one shared place.
